security_audit.summary: Static findings are false positives from Markdown formatting, documented protocols.io endpoints, and sample API requests. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, obfuscated logic, or unsafe shell execution was found in the reviewed files. Users should still protect OAuth tokens and confirm permissions before making legitimate API requests.

content.value_statement: Research teams need consistent API guidance for protocols, files, comments, and workspaces. This skill organizes protocols.io workflows for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Explains protocols.io authentication, OAuth token exchange, refresh tokens, and rate limit handling.
Provides endpoint guidance for searching, creating, updating, publishing, bookmarking, and exporting protocols.
Documents workspace operations, member roles, join requests, and workspace protocol workflows.
Covers protocol comments, threaded replies, step comments, and discussion monitoring.
Shows file upload, download, folder organization, metadata updates, and workspace storage practices.
Includes Python and curl examples for common protocols.io API requests.
limitations: Requires valid protocols.io API credentials and permissions supplied by the user.
Does not execute API requests by itself without an external tool or user-approved workflow.
API behavior, quotas, and endpoints may change after the skill content was written.
Does not validate scientific accuracy or laboratory safety of protocol contents.

use_cases.title: Find and Review Protocols
use_cases.description: Search public protocols, retrieve full details, review discussions, and prepare citation-ready references.

use_cases.title: Organize Lab Workspaces
use_cases.description: Plan workspace structure, manage protocol folders, handle member permissions, and attach experiment files.

use_cases.title: Build API Integrations
use_cases.description: Map authentication, endpoint flows, retries, pagination, and error handling for a protocols.io integration.

prompt_templates.title: Search Public Protocols
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me search protocols.io for public protocols about [topic]. Include useful filters, fields to review, and citation details to collect.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Draft Protocol
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through creating a new protocols.io draft for [method]. Include metadata, steps, materials, warnings, and review checks.

prompt_templates.title: Organize Workspace Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a protocols.io workspace folder plan for [project]. Include file naming, tags, upload order, metadata, and permission checks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an API Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a protocols.io API integration for [application]. Cover OAuth, endpoint sequence, pagination, rate limits, retries, file handling, and audit logging.

output_examples.input: Search for public CRISPR protocols and summarize what to inspect before using one.
output: A search plan using public protocol filters, keywords, and content format options.
A review checklist covering steps, materials, DOI, version, comments, and publication status.
A note to confirm laboratory safety and local approval before execution.

output_examples.input: Prepare a workspace plan for a lab moving protocols and files into protocols.io.
output: A folder structure for protocols, raw data, processed data, images, and documents.
Role guidance for owners, admins, members, and viewers.
File naming and metadata practices for searchable experiment records.

output_examples.input: Design an integration that uploads experiment results and records protocol runs.
output: An authenticated workflow for uploading files, checking upload status, and capturing file identifiers.
A run documentation plan with dates, status, modifications, results, and linked attachments.
Operational safeguards for rate limits, retries, permissions, and token storage.

best_practices: Store protocols.io tokens outside code and rotate them according to your organization policy.
Confirm workspace roles and protocol visibility before creating, publishing, uploading, or exporting content.
Use retries, backoff, pagination, and clear error handling for production API workflows.
anti_patterns: Do not paste access tokens into shared prompts, documents, logs, or version control.
Do not upload sensitive research data without approved consent, access controls, and retention rules.
Do not publish protocols before scientific, safety, and authorship review is complete.

faq.question: Does this skill call the protocols.io API directly?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. API calls require an available tool, credentials, and user approval.

faq.question: What credentials are needed?
faq.answer: You need a valid protocols.io access token or OAuth token with the required permissions.

faq.question: Can it manage private protocols?
faq.answer: Yes, if the supplied token has access to those private protocols or workspaces.

faq.question: Can it publish a protocol with a DOI?
faq.answer: It explains the publish workflow. You should review content and permissions before any publish request.

faq.question: Can it handle file uploads?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents upload endpoints, metadata, folders, verification, and file management practices.

faq.question: Does it check scientific safety?
faq.answer: No. A qualified reviewer must assess protocol safety, ethics, and scientific validity.
